title: Density of monic separable polynomials
statement: Let $F$ be a field equipped with a nontrivial real-valued nonarchimedean absolute value (multiplicative, zero exactly at zero, and satisfying $|x+y|\le\max(|x|,|y|)$). For every monic polynomial $f\in F[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] of degree $d\ge1$ and every real $\epsilon>0$, there exists a monic separable polynomial $g\in F[T]$ [def-pc-separable-polynomial] of degree $d$ such that $|g_i-f_i|<\epsilon$ for every coefficient $0\le i<d$. No completeness or perfectness of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: If $d=1$, monicity gives $f=T+f_0$. Its derivative is $1$, so $0\cdot f+1\cdot f\prime=1$ proves separability directly. Take $g=f$; every required coefficient difference is $0<\epsilon$. Henceforth suppose $d\ge2$.

proof.text:
Nontriviality supplies $u
e0$ with $|u|
e1$. Put $t=u$ if $|u|<1$ and $t=u^{-1}$ otherwise; multiplicativity gives $0<r=|t|<1$. The powers $t^n$ have strictly decreasing positive absolute values $r^n$, so are pairwise distinct. They are eventually smaller than any $\eta>0$: writing $c=r^{-1}-1>0$, induction gives $(1+c)^n\ge1+nc$, hence $r^n\le(1+nc)^{-1}<\eta$ for every sufficiently large integer $n$. Thus, for every finite subset $S\subset F$, there is a power $t^n
otin S$ with $0<|t^n|<\eta$: only finitely many of the distinct powers belong to $S$.

proof.text: There is at most one $a\in F$ with $f\prime+a=0$ as a polynomial: two such values would have difference the zero constant polynomial and so be equal. Use the preceding power construction with $\eta=\epsilon$ to choose $a$ outside this set and with $|a|<\epsilon$. Put $h=f+aT$. The coefficient formula for the derivative gives $h\prime=f\prime+a\ne0$. Since $d\ge2$, the added term has degree below $d$, so $h$ is still monic of degree $d$.

source.place: Agent proof of the auxiliary approximation lemma; formal derivative and separability convention: Tag 09H1 (fields-definition-separable), lines 1164–1178. The elementary absolute-value and coefficient calculations are supplied here, not asserted to be in Stacks.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-constant-shifts-finite-exceptions] to $h\in F[T]$ with $h\prime\ne0$. It gives a finite subset $B_h\subset F$ outside which $h+b$ is separable. Use the powers constructed in step 2, now with $S=B_h$ and $\eta=\epsilon$, to choose $b\notin B_h$ with $|b|<\epsilon$. Set $g=h+b=f+aT+b$. The cited statement gives that $g$ is separable.

proof.text: Both added terms have degree at most $1<d$, so the coefficient of $T^d$ in $g$ is $1$ and all coefficients above it remain zero. Thus $g$ is monic of degree $d$. The coefficient differences are $g_0-f_0=b$, $g_1-f_1=a$, and $g_i-f_i=0$ for $2\le i<d$. Their absolute values are respectively $|b|<\epsilon$, $|a|<\epsilon$, and $0<\epsilon$. This proves every required inequality. The construction took place entirely in $F$, with no completeness or perfectness assumption.
